name: daily-driver
notes: Promoted T1 -> T2 on 2026-07-27: the product is fully built (CLI + composite action.yml + 80 tests + CI with an action self-test lane) and is published for outside consumers, which is the durable-use trigger NEXT.md named. No production signals that would justify more: no deploys, no money, no user data, no secrets (the offline fake provider replays committed fixtures; the demo, tests and CI need no API key), so authority stays push free / merge free per owner directive agent-harness#91 -- the tier's gate does the verifying. Migrated from legacy .claude/tier.json, which was deleted in the same commit. sensitive_data stays false and must be re-reviewed the moment a real model-provider adapter lands (NEXT.md housekeeping trigger): keys will come from the environment only, never the repo. The deny floor is deliberately NOT vendored here; no Claude floor runs on DESKTOP-IHKOOJS (owner decisions 2026-09-07/09-20), so act as if nothing catches an irreversible command (Kraspyon keeps a user-scope hook, which a repo copy would double-spawn against). Committed .claude/settings.json keeps the allow and deny lists as the fresh-clone baseline but no defaultMode (removed 2026-10-03, claude-config#570): a project defaultMode would outrank the owner's user-settings bypass, so sessions follow the user's own permission mode.
